mcqs.learning_point: Recognise that compounds have fixed composition
mcqs.question: Which statement best compares the composition of a compound with that of an element?

options.A: Both have variable composition depending on their source.
options.B: Elements consist of only one type of atom, while compounds consist of two or more elements combined in a fixed ratio.
options.C: Compounds can have any proportion of constituent elements, whereas elements have a fixed composition.
options.D: Both compounds and elements can be separated into simpler substances by physical methods.

mcqs.answer: Elements consist of only one type of atom, while compounds consist of two or more elements combined in a fixed ratio.
mcqs.explanation: An element is made of only one kind of atom and cannot be broken down chemically. A compound is formed when two or more different elements chemically combine in a definite, fixed proportion (e.g., H₂O always has two hydrogen atoms for each oxygen atom). Options A, C and D contain incorrect statements about variability and separation methods.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly contrasts a compound with a mixture?

options.A: Water (H₂O) – a compound with fixed composition; Air – a mixture of gases with variable composition.
options.B: Sodium chloride – a mixture; Sand – a mixture of different minerals.
options.C: Carbon dioxide – an element; Coal – an element.
options.D: Iron – a compound; Steel – a compound.

mcqs.answer: Water (H₂O) – a compound with fixed composition; Air – a mixture of gases with variable composition.
mcqs.explanation: Water is a pure chemical compound whose molecules always contain two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Air is a physical mixture of gases (mainly N₂, O₂, Ar) whose relative proportions can vary. The other options misclassify substances: sodium chloride is a compound, not a mixture; carbon dioxide is a compound, not an element; iron is an element, and steel is an alloy (a mixture).

mcqs.question: An element is best defined as:

options.A: A pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
options.B: A substance composed of two or more types of atoms chemically combined.
options.C: A mixture of two or more pure substances.
options.D: A substance that can be separated by physical methods.

mcqs.answer: A pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
mcqs.explanation: Elements consist of only one kind of atom and cannot be chemically decomposed into simpler substances. Option B describes a compound, C describes a mixture, and D is incorrect because elements cannot be separated into simpler substances by any method, chemical or physical.

mcqs.question: A compound is:

options.A: A pure substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
options.B: A mixture of two or more elements that are not chemically combined.
options.C: A pure substance formed when two or more elements combine in a fixed proportion and can be separated only by chemical means.
options.D: A collection of atoms of the same element.

mcqs.answer: A pure substance formed when two or more elements combine in a fixed proportion and can be separated only by chemical means.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds are pure substances whose constituent elements are chemically bonded in a definite ratio (e.g., NaCl). They can be broken down only by chemical reactions. Option A defines an element, B defines a mixture, and D repeats the definition of an element.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an element from a compound?

options.A: Elements consist of only one type of atom; compounds consist of two or more different atoms chemically bonded in a fixed ratio.
options.B: Elements are always gases, whereas compounds are always solids.
options.C: Elements can be separated by physical methods; compounds cannot be separated at all.
options.D: Both elements and compounds have variable composition.

mcqs.answer: Elements consist of only one type of atom; compounds consist of two or more different atoms chemically bonded in a fixed ratio.
mcqs.explanation: An element is made of a single kind of atom (e.g., O₂). A compound contains atoms of different elements combined in a definite proportion (e.g., H₂O). Options B, C, and D contain false statements about states of matter, separation methods, and composition variability.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise that compounds have fixed composition
mcqs.question: A pure sample of glucose always contains 6 carbon, 12 hydrogen, and 6 oxygen atoms per molecule. Which statement reflects this property?

options.A: The composition of glucose can vary depending on the source.
options.B: The ratio of C:H:O in glucose is fixed at 1:2:1.
options.C: Glucose can be separated into carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen by simple filtration.
options.D: The mass of glucose changes with temperature.

mcqs.answer: The ratio of C:H:O in glucose is fixed at 1:2:1.
mcqs.explanation: Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) always has the same atomic ratio, demonstrating the fixed composition of a compound. Option A is false because composition does not vary. Option C is incorrect because chemical separation, not physical filtration, is required. Option D is unrelated to composition.

mcqs.question: Which pair correctly illustrates the difference between a compound and a mixture?
mcqs.explanation: Table salt is a pure chemical compound with a fixed composition (Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in a 1:1 ratio). Seawater is a mixture of water, salts, and other substances whose proportions can vary. The other options either list two substances of the same category or do not provide a clear compound‑mixture contrast.

mcqs.question: A jeweler examines a piece of pure gold. Which description best matches this substance?

options.A: It is made of only gold atoms and cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
options.B: It is a combination of gold and silver atoms in varying proportions.
options.C: It can be separated into gold and copper by filtration.
options.D: It consists of gold atoms chemically bonded with oxygen.

mcqs.answer: It is made of only gold atoms and cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
mcqs.explanation: Pure gold is an element; it consists solely of gold atoms and cannot be chemically decomposed into simpler substances. Options B, C, and D describe alloys, physical separation, or a compound, none of which apply to elemental gold.
